title: Risk of suicidality in clinical trials of antidepressants in adults: analysis of proprietary data submitted to US Food and Drug Administration
authors: Stone M, Laughren T, Jones ML, Levenson M, Holland PC, Hughes A, et al.
followUp: double-blind treatment periods of the trials
population: Adults in 372 double-blind placebo-controlled trials of 11 antidepressants for any indication, with individual data submitted by sponsors to the FDA in 2005 and 2006; analysis by FDA staff
funder: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. All authors were FDA employees.
result: In psychiatric indications, suicidal behaviour or ideation OR 1.62 (95% CI 0.97 to 2.71) and suicidal behaviour OR 2.30 (1.04 to 5.09) under age 25; 0.79 (0.64 to 0.98) and 0.87 (0.58 to 1.29) at 25 to 64; 0.37 (0.18 to 0.76) and 0.06 (0.01 to 0.58) at 65 or older; the OR declined by 2.6% per year of age. Sertraline in adults with psychiatric disorders: ideation or worse in 18 of 6363 against 28 of 5081 on placebo, OR 0.51 (0.29 to 0.91), risk difference -2.50 per 1000.
